newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet hopes to add 10-15 planes.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet hopes to add 10-15 planes.

text.p: ValuJet Inc President Lewis Jordan said on Tuesday that the low-cost carrier hopes to add another 10-15 planes to its service between mid-December and mid-March.
But he told reporters in a conference call that the airline had yet to recieve the necessary federal government approval for such a move.

Another 15 aircraft, which the airline has no immediate plans to begin flying, will be offered for service in the form of 12 month lease agreements to curtail the amount of cost to ValuJet's balance sheet.
ValuJet has given the U.S. Department a required notice of 45 days that it plans to begin adding more aircraft to service in mid-December.
The company also has begun preliminary discussions with the Federal Aviation System on an evaluation system that could be used by regulators to determine if additional aircraft are justified.
But Jordan said no formal application has yet been made to the FAA.

"It is our plan, in general, to phase those planes in from approximately mid-December to approximately mid-March. And we anticipate, or are hopeful of, FAA approval. But there can be no assurance of that until we actually make application," the executive said.
"A few airplanes might be added in the mid-December timeframe to give us an additional boost in ability to accommodate holiday season traffic," he added.
The addition of 15 aircraft would bring ValuJet to a level of operation at which executives believe it can again begin to generate profits.

"In general we have said we probably would need to be in the 30 airplane range before we could resume consistent profitability," Jordan noted. In the past, the addition of a single aicraft has meant the simultaneous addition of a new destination to scheduled service. But Jordan said no plans to add new cities have been made and intimated that initial additions of aircraft would be used to increase the frequency of flights to the airline's most popular destinations.

"Since the first 15 are up and operating and doing quite well by the way, we believe the best way for us to go forward is to take the next 10 or 15 and present them to the FAA with a specific operating plan on a phase-in schedule," Jordan said.

"The FAA have said to us that they will look at any proposed measuring stick or report card method by which we believe we can justify or substantiate the additional aircraft coming up into our service. At the moment, I think they are very pleased with what they're seeing."
